NVDA.text: Nvidia finished essentially flat and outperformed a 0.6% Nasdaq decline as investors digested its newly announced $500 billion-plus compute-financing partnerships; no clearer stock-specific catalyst emerged.

AVGO.text: Broadcom fell about 1.5% with the weaker technology tape as fading U.S.-Iran deal hopes lifted oil and pressured the Nasdaq; no distinct Broadcom-specific catalyst was confirmed.

TSM.text: TSM gained about 0.9% and outperformed the falling Nasdaq, with recent strong July sales still supportive and no fresh company-specific catalyst confirmed during Tuesday's risk-off market session.

ASML.text: ASML rose about 3.8% despite a lower Nasdaq; no fresh ASML-specific catalyst was confirmed, and the move appears to reflect a semiconductor-equipment rebound within an otherwise mixed technology session.

KLAC.text: KLA rose about 4.0% despite the Nasdaq decline, with no confirmed company-specific catalyst; the move appears to have been part of relative strength in semiconductor shares during the session.

INTC.text: Intel edged up about 0.2% after completing a $20 billion share sale, stabilizing after Monday's dilution-driven drop as investors absorbed the newly raised capital.

MU.text: Micron gained about 0.9% while the Nasdaq fell, with no confirmed Micron-specific catalyst; the move appears to have reflected relative strength in semiconductor shares during the session.

DDOG.text: Datadog fell about 5.4%, giving back part of Monday's sharp rebound with no new catalyst confirmed as trading remained dominated by the prior earnings reaction and concerns about its modest sequential growth outlook.

META.text: Meta gained about 0.7% and outperformed the Nasdaq's 0.6% decline, with no confirmed market-moving company catalyst; the move was modest enough to look like ordinary stock-specific resilience.

PLTR.text: Palantir finished essentially flat, slipping about 0.2%, with no fresh company-specific catalyst confirmed after the prior week's earnings-driven surge.

SPCX.text: SpaceX fell about 3.9% back below its $135 IPO price, ending a three-day rally as investors took profits amid continuing lockup-supply concerns and weaker results from satellite-broadband peer AST SpaceMobile.
